The supplied papers do not address AI consciousness or self-awareness directly. They focus on AI methods for wind, weather, and energy forecasting, benchmarking, and monitoring rather than questions about whether AI systems are conscious or self-aware. [1-10]

At most, some papers mention technical ideas like self-attention, self-supervised learning, or explainability, but only as modeling tools for forecasting and inverse problems, not as evidence or discussion of consciousness or self-awareness. For example, the papers cover transformer self-attention for structural health monitoring [1], self-supervised atmospheric and wind nowcasting models [3, 9, 10], and generative AI used strictly as an explainability layer in energy forecasting [6].
